summary: Tested the new POST /api/support endpoint (Emergent managed email relay via Resend proxy) and the frontend /support screen. Backend: created /app/backend/tests/test_support.py (pytest, 7 tests) - ALL 7 PASSED (2 happy paths + 5 validation-rejection cases). Confirmed happy paths (message only, message + delivered@resend.dev) return {accepted:true} with HTTP 200; empty message, missing message, invalid reply_email, unknown extra field, and whitespace-only message all correctly return HTTP 400. Frontend: reached /support via the Main Menu Support button (direct navigation to /support redirects to '/' because the app manages routing through the main menu), typed an invalid email 'not-an-email' + a message and tapped send-message-button — the validation error 'Enter a valid email address or leave this field empty.' rendered, and success-message did NOT appear (no network call fired). Cleared the email field and tapped Send again — success-message testID rendered with the exact text 'Message submitted!' and the follow-up 'Thank you for your feedback!' plus the Send another button. Total backend send calls during this run: 2 (well under the 10/hour process quota).

minor.issue: Rate-limit slot (attempts.append) is consumed BEFORE Pydantic validation in submit_support (support_mail.py:190 vs 198). Malformed/validation-failing requests also count against the 10/hour process quota, so an abusive/broken client can exhaust the quota with 400s. Consider incrementing the counter only after successful validation (or only after successful proxy send).

action_items: OPTIONAL: Move the rate-limit slot allocation in submit_support (support_mail.py) to AFTER successful validation so 400-generating requests don't burn quota.

OPTIONAL doc: /support route redirects to '/' if reached directly (deep-link). If deep-link should work standalone, register a proper Expo Router route guard; otherwise fine as-is because Support is only entered from the Main Menu button in-app.
critical_code_review_comments: support_mail.py:31-32 uses os.environ['EMERGENT_EMAIL_KEY'] / ['EMAIL_FROM_NAME'] which will crash on import if either is missing. Good fail-fast pattern, matches project convention.
support_mail.py:36 SUPPORT_ADDRESS is a server-side constant, never caller-controlled — correctly avoids open-relay risk.
support_mail.py:47 screenshot field is accepted for backward compat and intentionally NOT forwarded to the email service — verified: only presence is signalled via a note in the HTML.

support_mail.py:99-123 _assert_safe_email enforces Emergent email guardrails (no forms, no credential-asking phrases, https-only links, no shorteners/IP hosts, anchor-text/href host parity) — correctly called for every send.

support_mail.py:126-145 send_email raises HTTPException(502) on proxy 4xx/5xx and HTTPException(500) on transport errors; confirmation-email failure is caught and logged so the main support request still returns 200 — good UX.
support.tsx:55-59 frontend refuses to send unless EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL is defined and https:// — good hardening.
support.tsx:66-88 correctly parses response, checks accepted===true, transitions to sent state and clears form fields; preserves draft on failure via the error branch.
seed_data_creation: None. Backend sends went to fixed owner arcades.soijanda@gmail.com and confirmation to delivered@resend.dev (Resend test address); 2 successful sends during the run.
context_for_next_testing_agent: POST /api/support is fully working via Emergent managed email (Resend proxy). Rate limit is 10/hour per backend process; validation failures also count toward the quota (minor issue noted). Frontend /support screen is only reachable via the Main Menu Support button, direct URL navigation redirects to '/' — factor this into any future automation. testIDs available on the Support screen: back-button, support-message-input, support-email-input, add-screenshot-button, send-message-button, success-message, send-another-button. Always use delivered@resend.dev as the reply_email during automated testing to avoid real inboxes.
rca_of_issue: N/A — no regression, feature implementation verified working end-to-end.
